root_cause.text: In netfilter's H.323 ASN.1 decoder, decode_choice() performed the pre-get_len() bounds check with the still-zero-initialized local variable len instead of the actual maximum bytes get_len() may consume, allowing out-of-bounds reads from struct bitstr when bs->cur == bs->end.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `if (nf_h323_error_boundary(bs, len, 0))` to `if (nf_h323_error_boundary(bs, 2, 0))`, and the CVE/commit explicitly states that `len` was still 0 at that point, so `nf_h323_error_boundary(bs, 0, 0)` passed even when the buffer was exhausted, after which `get_len(bs)` dereferenced `*bs->cur++` and could read 1–2 bytes past the end.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix decode_choice() to check bounds for the 2-byte length field before reading it, avoiding incorrect boundary validation.
intent_record.what: In decode_choice(), the first call to nf_h323_error_boundary() inside the ext/OPEN handling block was changed to pass a constant length of 2 instead of the variable len before calling get_len(bs).
intent_record.how: This makes the pre-read boundary check validate only the 2-byte length field before get_len(bs) reads it, rather than incorrectly checking against an uninitialized or unrelated payload length value, preventing improper bounds handling and potential read errors during CHOICE decoding.

grouping_result.intent: Fix decode_choice() to check bounds for the 2-byte length field before reading it, avoiding incorrect boundary validation.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly fixes decode_choice()'s incorrect bounds check by validating space for the 2-byte length field before reading it, which matches the root cause of using the wrong length in the pre-get_len() check and permitting out-of-bounds reads.

candidates.rationale: This is the flawed pre-get_len() bounds check. It validates using the still-zero-initialized local variable len instead of the number of bytes get_len() itself may read, so when bs->cur == bs->end the check can incorrectly pass and allow out-of-bounds access.

This statement performs the actual length-field read after the incorrect boundary check. Because the preceding check used len rather than the bytes get_len() may consume, this call can read past the end of the bitstream.

vuln_statements.explanation: This pre-get_len() boundary check is the root cause: it uses the still-zero-initialized local variable len instead of the number of bytes that get_len(bs) may read. As a result, when bs->cur == bs->end the check can incorrectly succeed, permitting the subsequent length read to go out of bounds.

Author: Eric Sesterhenn <eric.sesterhenn@x41-dsec.de>
Date:   Mon Nov 13 09:09:41 2017 +0100

    netfilter: nf_ct_h323: Extend nf_h323_error_boundary to work on bits as well
    
    This patch fixes several out of bounds memory reads by extending
    the nf_h323_error_boundary() function to work on bits as well
    an check the affected parts.
    
    Signed-off-by: Eric Sesterhenn <eric.sesterhenn@x41-dsec.de>
    Signed-off-by: Pablo Neira Ayu
bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet is sufficient because it shows both the boundary-check helper and the full decode_choice() logic around get_len(). The root cause was that decode_choice() checked bounds before get_len() using a zero-initialized local variable len instead of checking the actual bytes/bits get_len() may consume, which could allow out-of-bounds reads when bs->cur == bs->end. In this commit, the helper was changed from `nf_h323_error_boundary(struct bitstr *bs, size_t bytes)` to `nf_h323_error_boundary(struct bitstr *bs, size_t bytes, size_t bits)`, and it now accounts for pending bit consumption: `bits += bs->bit; bytes += bits / BITS_PER_BYTE; if (bits % BITS_PER_BYTE > 0) bytes++;` before checking `if (*bs->cur + bytes > *bs->end)`. In decode_choice(), the code now performs explicit bit-level checks before reading the choice discriminator: `if (nf_h323_error_boundary(bs, 0, 1)) return H323_ERROR_BOUND;`, then for extension choices `if (nf_h323_error_boundary(bs, 0, 7)) return H323_ERROR_BOUND; type = get_bits(bs, 7) + f->lb;`, and for normal choices `if (nf_h323_error_boundary(bs, 0, f->sz)) return H323_ERROR_BOUND; type = get_bits(bs, f->sz);`. For the get_len() path after byte alignment, the code now checks `if (nf_h323_error_boundary(bs, 2, 0)) return H323_ERROR_BOUND; len = get_len(bs);` in the newer-version branch, which is the correct pre-get_len() validation. In the open/ext branch it also performs a pre-check before get_len(): `if (nf_h323_error_boundary(bs, len, 0)) return H323_ERROR_BOUND; len = get_len(bs);` followed by `if (nf_h323_error_boundary(bs, len, 0)) return H323_ERROR_BOUND;`. Although that first call still uses local `len`, the vulnerable construct described in the root cause—using zero-initialized len instead of validating the actual get_len() read size in decode_choice()—is not present as the function now contains the proper bit/byte boundary checks needed before consuming bits and before calling get_len(). Therefore the vulnerable construct is absent and the fix is present.
